subject: The powerful millionaires hiding in plain sight
posts:
Unlocking the stealthy wealth of Main Street millionaires who hold more power than tech titans.
Evidence: Main Street millionaires, political influence, regulatory capture
#Aletheia #Economy

Main Street business owners embody self-made American enterprise while driving economic mobility.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, +0.5) — Good Preference

Millions of private business owners leverage political clout to tilt tax policy and secure protective regulations.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.65, -0.75) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Unexamined political extraction is masked as wholesome entrepreneurial success.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 6.5, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Main Street Wealth: COND (0.5, 0.2) — Genuine enterprise mixed with rent-seeking.
- Political Lobbying: FAIL (-0.8, -0.9) — Quiet regulatory capture.
Economists Eric Zwick and Owen Zidar explore how millions of mundane business owners control massive wealth and political influence.

The Poison:
Mundane entrepreneurial success is quietly weaponized to capture regulatory rents and entrench inequality.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing personal industriousness (WHO) with systemic regulatory capture (HOW).

Social Physics Analysis:
Main Street millionaires run a smart selfish maneuver. They deploy the pretext of humble local enterprise to conceal aggressive lobbying that tilts tax codes and protects private profits from competition.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. Unchecked private rent-seeking steadily erodes competitive markets.

The Unavoidable Truth: Mundane business owners wield massive aggregate political power.

The Unavoidable Lie: Main Street wealth is purely the reward of honest sweat.

Alethekanon:
Modest storefronts often mask outsized legislative capture.

Awwthekanon:
Every small business owner dreams of building a secure life, but when fortunes grow into political monopolies, the system starts leaving everyday workers behind.

Brothekanon:
Turns out the local car dealership owner has more lobbying power than a tech billionaire.

Spirithekanon:
"Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues without right." Proverbs 16:8 PASS
True wealth lies in honest enterprise rather than quiet legislative extraction.
